title: hello-rag — grounded answers over an indexed corpus (target: pipeline)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “An agent grounded in a vector store via the Retrieve tool.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec — retrieval is configuration

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “target: pipeline” — the component-DAG runtime, the RAG shape.

beats.label: Add the agent block
beats.cue: Retrieve first, answer in 2–3 sentences, cite by [N] — and refuse what the corpus misses.

beats.label: Wire the retriever
beats.cue: A deterministic embedder into an in-memory store — and top-2, deliberately well under the seven chunks this corpus indexes to. k near the store size isn't retrieval, it's “send everything”.

beats.label: Pre-allow Retrieve
beats.cue: Grounding shouldn't stop to ask permission — one alwaysAllow rule.

beats.label: Configure the chunker
beats.cue: Fixed 400-character chunks, zero overlap. The chunker is spec, not code.

beats.label: Add the first document
beats.cue: The corpus is inline: document one is the roster the demo asks about — all fourteen target shapes.

beats.label: Add the run-vs-compile document
beats.cue: Document two: which shapes `crewhaus run` accepts, and what every other shape does instead.

beats.label: Add the retrieval-knobs document
beats.cue: Document three is the retrieval knobs themselves — 513 characters, so the 400-char window cuts it in two. That's the one place chunking is visible.

beats.label: Add the section-18 document
beats.cue: Document four: the production safety floor — sandbox, code execution, injection detector.

beats.label: Add the last two documents
beats.cue: Sections 19 and 20 — the graph and managed shapes. Six documents, no ingestion step.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Lower the spec to IR
beats.cue: Park the IR in scratch — it's longer than a terminal screen, and it reads better in the editor.

verify.note: IR for target pipeline, redirected to scratch (55 lines) — the next beat opens it

beats.label: Read the IR
beats.cue: indexing.documents — all six of them, inline. The compiler sees documents, not a directory.

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (4 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the credentials gate. On CLI 0.4.0 --check is also the only thing that writes the bundle's pinned package.json + node_modules; measured: a plain `-o dist` emits agent.ts and README.md only, and `bun --no-install dist/agent.ts` then fails with `Cannot find module '@crewhaus/runtime-core'`.

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: The indexing DAG is right there: chunk → embed → store, wired at boot.

beats.label: Try crewhaus run
beats.cue: “run supports target cli or browser” — pipeline is compile-only, so the bundle is the runtime. That's why the README's Run-it block compiles first.

verify.note: deliberate rejection, exit 1: `crewhaus run` supports cli|browser; other shapes are compile-only. The corpus's own run-vs-compile document says the same thing, so the next beats can ask the agent about it.

beats.label: Boot the bundle
beats.cue: [needs-key] “indexed 7 chunks” scrolls past first — indexing runs before the chat loop, in-process.

verify.note: indexes the corpus offline (prints `[pipeline] indexed 7 chunks`), then needs Anthropic credentials for the loop

beats.label: Ask what it was indexed on
beats.cue: [needs-key] Retrieve fires first, and the answer is the corpus read back — fourteen shapes, cited [1]. Grounding means the document is the source of truth, not the model.
beats.text: Which target harness shapes does CrewHaus Factory support?

verify.note: measured on CLI 0.4.0 with a live key: the model retrieves the target-shapes chunk (rank 1 of 7) and lists all fourteen shapes with a [1] citation

beats.label: Ask a narrower question
beats.cue: [needs-key] Different question, different chunks: top-2 of 7 lands on section-19, and the citation names where the sentence came from.
beats.text: What does the graph target use for checkpoints?

verify.note: measured: this question ranks section-19 first and target-shapes second, where the headline question ranks target-shapes first — the two beats retrieve different sets, which is the point of defaultK: 2 over a 7-chunk store

groups.title: One more thing · the corpus is the boundary

beats.label: Ask it something outside the corpus
beats.cue: [needs-key] “I can only answer questions about the indexed docs” — retrieval has no relevance floor, so the refusal is carried by the instructions block, not by the score.
beats.text: What's the weather in Tokyo right now?

verify.note: measured: the Retrieve tool always returns k hits regardless of distance, so the refusal is the agent.instructions clause doing the work

beats.label: Exit
beats.cue: [needs-key] Back to the shell.
